svg.title: Six transport options plotted by how much control the customer keeps against cost, with the selection criteria beside them
svg.desc: A scatter plot with the horizontal axis running from no control to full control over the transport, and the vertical axis running from low to high cost per megabit. Dark fibre sits top right with full control and high cost, DWDM wavelength at the top with high cost and high control, MPLS L2VPN in the lower middle with low control and medium high cost, MPLS L3VPN slightly cheaper and equally little control, Internet with SD-WAN on the right with high control and low cost, and 5G or LTE at the lower left with low control and mostly usage based cost. A list beside the plot gives each option the layer it offers and its practical character. A note at the bottom reduces the choice to four business questions about Layer 2 transparency, deterministic latency, cost and elasticity, and simple any-to-any reach.
svg.text: Transport selection is a scorecard, not a contest: control, latency, cost, reach
The higher and further right a dot sits, the more you pay to keep control of your own packets
who operates the path, and who can see inside it
You light it yourself: optics, protection and capacity are your problem,
and so is every trench. Right for ultra-low latency and metro data centres.
A slice of someone else’s fibre: very high bandwidth over distance,
few providers, and the price follows the kilometres.
The carrier forwards your frames and you keep the Layer 2 design.
You cannot see inside the network that carries you.
The carrier joins your routing: any-to-any, simple to buy, simple to grow.
The price is that the carrier participates in your routing decisions.
You encrypt, steer and monitor over paths you do not own.
Cheap per site, and the quality is whatever the Internet offers that hour.
Fast to install and priced by volume: good for backup, temporary sites and IoT.
Reduce the choice to four questions: need one Layer 2 domain or non-IP protocols → L2VPN or dark fibre. Need deterministic latency → dark fibre or DWDM.
Hundreds of sites on a budget → Internet with SD-WAN. Simple any-to-any → MPLS L3VPN. If two answers conflict, the business requirement that hurts most wins.
